Section 3.2 forbids using Outputs "to create models or services that directly compete with Holymolly and its models, products and services. However, that you may use Outputs for lawful commercial or non-commercial purposes, so long as such Outputs are not distributed or made available to third parties in a manner inconsistent with this Agreement or applicable laws;" and forbids to "make the Generative 3D Foundation Model Service available to any third party, including end users, without the prior written authorization and consent of Holymolly." Outputs are defined as "outputs generated by our Services including all operations, edits, results and any processing performed after your input", so a rigged or animated mesh is an Output and the mesh you send is an Input. Section 5.2.2 makes Paid Users' rights subject to "the consent and authorization to authorize the Company to use and display the Inputs and Outputs as may be necessary for Service provision on royalty-free, perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, non-exclusive basis"; the help centre narrows this to "If you set your model to "public,"" but the terms do not. For this repo that means every character mesh uploaded for rigging is licensed to Tripo perpetually and irrevocably, and offering the Tripo-backed pipeline to outsiders, through the repo's MCP server for instance, would need written consent.

Name matching cannot do it: UniRig's Apply Animation node refuses anything without mixamorig: names and copies curves by name with no rest-pose handling (VMC-035), and articulationxl rigs are bone_0 to bone_N (VMC-036). Three differences the role-keyed Blender retarget must absorb: rest pose (the BVH frame 0 T-pose faces +Z with the arms 8 degrees below level and the thighs splayed 21 degrees, the FBX rest is a T-pose facing -Y, while the articulationxl rigs have the arms hanging), so a per-bone offset is computed from frame 0 or the rest pose before Copy Rotation and baking; scale (BVH in CMU's ASF units, 0.056444 per metre, FBX in centimetres, rigs 1.84 to 2.11 units tall), so hip translation is scaled by leg length; and units of time (120 fps BVH, 30 fps FBX). Then clean-up on raw takes that were never loops: trim to a cycle, graph.butterworth_smooth and graph.euler_filter for the joint flips the Daz README describes ("The data was never cleaned and contains a wide variety of joint-flipping problems"), and foot pinning, which nothing in the repo does. Blender 4.5.9 in the image imports BVH and FBX (VMC-035 and the note's Clean-up section). No GPU memory is involved.

FBX (io_scene_fbx/export_fbx_bin.py; "Write a FBX file") with bake_anim ("Export baked keyframe animation", default True) samples at bake_anim_step (default 1.0 frame) with scene.frame_set and reads each bone as "par_mat_inv @ self._ref.pose.bones[self.bdata.name].matrix" (fbx_utils.py get_matrix_local, the "current pose" branch), with bake_anim_use_all_actions ("Export each action as a separated FBX's AnimStack, instead of global scene animation", default True), bake_anim_use_nla_strips, bake_anim_force_startend_keying ("Always add a keyframe at start and end of actions for animated channels") and bake_anim_simplify_factor (default 1.0, "0.0 to disable"); the manual's page for these options reads ".. todo:: Add this information." for all but All Actions. glTF (io_scene_gltf2; "Export scene as glTF 2.0 file") with export_force_sampling ("Apply sampling to all animations", default True) steps "bpy.context.scene.frame_set(int(frame))" in sampling_cache.py and reads "blender_bone.bone.matrix_local.inverted_safe() @ blender_bone.matrix"; export_animation_mode defaults to ACTIONS ("Export actions (actives and on NLA tracks) as separate animations"), export_bake_animation is "Force exporting animation on every object. Can be useful when using constraints or driver", export_rest_position_armature defaults True, and the manual notes "Set all glTF Animation starting at 0. Can be useful for looping animation". The image's default scene is 24 fps (fps_base 1.0), frames 1 to 250. Bone names pass through unchanged in all three, so bone_N names survive; which format a game engine needs was not decided here.

The manual at branch blender-v4.5-release (manual/animation/constraints/tracking/ik_solver.rst) says "The Inverse Kinematics constraint implements the inverse kinematics armature posing technique. Hence, it is only available for bones.", with Chain Length "How many bones are included in the IK effect. Set to 0 to include all bones.", Use Tail "Include bone's tail as last element in chain.", Pole Target "Object for pole rotation.", Iterations "Maximum number of solving iterations." and Influence "Controls the percentage of affect the constraint has on the object."; the RNA adds use_location "Chain follows position of target" and use_rotation "Chain follows rotation of target". Copy Rotation (manual/animation/constraints/transform/copy_rotation.rst) "forces its owner to match the rotation of its target", with Mix modes Replace, Add, Before Original ("as if it was applied to a parent"), After Original and Offset (Legacy). Pinning a planted foot would be an IK constraint on the shin bone (chain_count 2, target an empty or helper bone at the contact point, influence keyed 1 on contact frames and 0 elsewhere), baked with visual_keying and clear_constraints, the chain coming from the thigh, shin, foot and toe roles that scripts/bone_roles.py map finds. Nothing of this is written or run; docs/guide/animation.md records that on the walk's contact frames the lowest foot or toe bone end sits 0.026 to 0.100 units above where it rests, which is what pinning would address.

claims.claim: At 4e426f5 the model takes an English text prompt (README: 'For optimal results, keep your prompt under 60 words.') and a duration in seconds. MotionFlowMatching.generate computes length = int(round(duration_slider * self.output_mesh_fps)), where config.yml sets output_mesh_fps: 30 and train_frames: 360, and clamps length to between min(train_frames, 20) and train_frames, so a clip is 20 to 360 frames, 0.67 to 12 s, at 30 fps; the paper says 'All motions were resampled to 30 fps', and the only 20 fps figure in the code is a comment inside a self-test routine in t2m_runtime.py ('assuming 30fps output, 20fps internal'), not the generate path. Each frame is a 201-value vector (paper: root translation 3, body orientation 6, 21 local joint rotations in 6D and 22 joint positions). The sampler returns, per sample, latent_denorm (L, 201), keypoints3d (L, 52, 3), rot6d (L, 52, 6), transl (L, 3) and root_rotations_mat (L, 3, 3), after slerp smoothing of the first 22 joints, Savitzky-Golay smoothing of translation and grounding on the template mesh's lowest vertex; with 52 joints the DiT emits 21 body plus 15 and 15 finger rotations. With fbxsdkpy importable, local_infer.py writes one FBX per seed (default --num_seeds 4) plus a .txt of the prompt; SMPLH2WoodFBX converts axis-angle poses (L, 52, 3) to rotation matrices, keys each joint's LclRotation as XYZ Euler degrees (transforms3d mat2euler, axes sxyz) and the Pelvis LclTranslation at scale 100 (metres to centimetres), at fps=30, onto assets/wooden_models/boy_Rigging_smplx_tex.fbx; without fbxsdkpy the output falls back to 'dict'. The wrappers' Save NPZ nodes write keypoints3d, rot6d, transl, root_rotations_mat, text, duration and seed, and Aero-Ex's adds poses (T, 156).

In its name-matching phase the code then skips every alias that starts with bone_ except bone_0 ('# Skip unstable UniRig indices for name matching'), so on a UniRig target only the pelvis is matched by name; that rule also applies to a user mapping_file unless it sets rokoko_custom_names, so a map written from this repo's bone_roles.py roles would be ignored as the code stands. The remaining bones go through 'Phase 2: Structural BFS Matching (Hierarchy-Aware)' from the two roots with geometric and single-child fallbacks, 'Phase 4: Arm Fallback Detection (Now with Topological Wrist Search)' and finger matching relative to the wrist; the README calls this 'UniRig/ArticulationXL: Built-in support for UniRig-detected skeletons.' This repo's articulationxl rigs have 24 to 47 bones with per-figure numbering, so the fixed map would mostly miss and the structural matching would decide the result. Not run.

Read from Aeroplane_FW.bvh (5,554,423 bytes, 7,869 frames) and Aeroplane_ID.bvh (1,262,991 bytes, 1,792 frames), downloaded on 2026-10-02 from the page's per-file table: ROOT Hips with "CHANNELS 6 Xposition Yposition Zposition Yrotation Xrotation Zrotation", 22 JOINTs each with "CHANNELS 3 Yrotation Xrotation Zrotation", 72 values per frame, "Frame Time: 0.016667" (60 fps), offsets in centimetres (thigh 43.74, shin 43.21, hips at y 95 to 99 across the first 400 frames; the paper's actor is 182 cm), Y up, toes along +Z, and a zero-rotation rest pose that is a T-pose with the arms along the X axis (RightShoulder OFFSET -15.79 0 0, RightElbow -31.15 0 0, RightWrist -25.54 0 0). Joint names: Hips, Chest, Chest2, Chest3, Chest4, Neck, Head, RightCollar, RightShoulder, RightElbow, RightWrist, LeftCollar, LeftShoulder, LeftElbow, LeftWrist, RightHip, RightKnee, RightAnkle, RightToe, LeftHip, LeftKnee, LeftAnkle, LeftToe; End Sites below Head, both wrists and both toes. Each joint is named for the joint at its bone's start, so RightShoulder is the upper arm, RightElbow the forearm, RightWrist the hand, RightHip the thigh, RightKnee the shin and RightAnkle the foot. There are no finger joints: the paper says the data excludes "finger transformations". The recorded T-pose frames are not zero rotations: among the first 400 frames of Aeroplane_FW.bvh the smallest combined limb rotation is 54.6 degrees (frame 225), so the OFFSET-defined rest, not a chosen frame, is the reference pose for any retarget.
claims.as_first_reported: BVH at 60 fps from an Xsens suit, 'a 28 bone skeleton' (hips, spine, chest, neck, head, collarbones, shoulders, elbows, wrists, legs).

claims.claim: A 100STYLE source clip would reach an articulationxl bone_N rig through the role-keyed retarget the video-mocap note already names as unbuilt (VMC-050), and the 23 source joints map onto scripts/bone_roles.py's roles with nothing left over on either side except the rig's optional hip and head_end: Hips to pelvis (the root on articulationxl rigs); Chest, Chest2, Chest3, Chest4 to the spine chain ending at chest (the rig's own spine count varies, so the four source bones must be distributed or compressed onto spine, spine_2 ... chest by order); Neck to neck; Head to head; RightCollar to right_shoulder; RightShoulder to right_upper_arm; RightElbow to right_forearm; RightWrist to right_hand; RightHip to right_thigh; RightKnee to right_shin; RightAnkle to right_foot; RightToe to right_toe; the same on the left. Three things the retarget must handle, read from the files and the docstring and not tried: the source rest is a T-pose while articulationxl rigs rest with the arms hanging, so each frame's rotation is a delta from the source rest applied in world space onto the target rest; the source is in centimetres with hips at about 97, so root translation scales by the hip-height ratio; and the recorded T-pose frames are not zero rotations, so the OFFSET rest is the reference. The original BVH is the simpler source for this: world-aligned offsets, one joint per role; orangeduck's 75-joint version adds 52 finger and end joints that carry no motion and a joint-oriented rest that needs Geno_bind.bvh to interpret. UniRig's Apply Animation applies to neither: both lack mixamorig: names.

Section 3(b) requires an Adaptation to take "reasonable steps to clearly label, demarcate or otherwise identify that changes were made to the original Work. For example ... a modification could indicate 'The original work has been modified.'". Section 4(c): "You must not distort, mutilate, modify or take other derogatory action in relation to the Work which would be prejudicial to the Original Author's honor or reputation." Section 4(a), which applies to copies of the Work, adds "You must include a copy of, or the Uniform Resource Identifier (URI) for, this License with every copy of the Work You Distribute", "You may not sublicense the Work", and that a Collection need not itself be put under the licence: "this does not require the Collection apart from the Work itself to be made subject to the terms of this License." Section 7(a): the licence terminates "automatically upon any breach by You of the terms". A retargeted clip falls under the definition of Adaptation, "any other form in which the Work may be recast, transformed, or adapted including in any form recognizably derived from the original"; whether a clip baked onto another rig is also a "copy of the Work" for 4(a) is not settled here, so a credit line that carries the author, title, URI, the licence URI and the word modified satisfies both readings: "Open Motion Project by ACCAD/The Ohio State University, CC BY 3.0 (creativecommons.org/licenses/by/3.0/), accad.osu.edu/research/motion-lab/mocap-system-and-data, modified."

claims.candidate: Rig Bridge (Blender Extensions id humanoid_remap_studio; GitHub qw424886884/rig-bridge; by Feng Ji Shi)
claims.claim: How Rig Bridge recognises a rig, read at cd615a4, with one measurement. Three routes feed every role: preset bone-name tables (eight families; accepted when PRESET_MIN_CONFIDENCE 0.32, PRESET_MIN_CORE_HITS 4 and a signature gap of 0.08 are met), semantic names (HRS_SEMANTIC_NAME_MIN_SCORE 0.68, with aliases such as hips, pelvis, root, thigh, calf, shin, forearm, mixamorig: stripped), and topology (armature_scan.analyze_humanoid_roles: an axis model from bone spans, bilateral limb landmarks, paired leg chains, a trunk chain split into spine, neck and head, arm chains with an optional shoulder, and finger fans). merged_role_matches_for_armature takes preset, then name, then topology when the armature matched a preset, and topology, then name, then preset when it did not and core_topology_coverage is ready. Fifteen core roles are mandatory (CORE_REMAP_ROLE_IDS: hips, spine_01, head, and per side upper_arm, lower_arm, hand, upper_leg, lower_leg, foot), each needing score >= 0.56 (HRS_STRUCTURAL_CORE_MIN_SCORE) on a non-preset route, a unique bone, and the expected parent chains (spine_01 under hips, head under spine_01, lower_arm under upper_arm, hand under lower_arm, upper_leg under hips, lower_leg under upper_leg, foot under lower_leg); the topology scan scores hips 0.86 from a paired-leg root, spine 0.72 to 0.74, neck 0.68, head 0.76, legs 0.79 (toes 0.62), arms 0.68 (hands 0.62), fingers 0.48. When coverage fails, update_auto_summary writes "No stable automatic workflow was found. Confirm that both rigs are humanoid armatures." and execute_retarget cancels with the same text; bake_retarget_action raises "Insufficient core mapping: n/15". Measured on this host on 2026-10-02 by importing matcher.py and preset_catalog.py from cd615a4 as a stub package (both import only `re`): for bone_0 to bone_39 against all 35 roles, score_name_for_role returned at most 0.1, best_matching_preset returned None and classify_bone_names returned status "no-preset-hit", while a 22-name Mixamo control list matched preset "mixamo". So an articulationxl rig can be accepted only by the topology route, or by slots a script fills; its names carry nothing.

claims.claim: Rig Bridge gates on rest pose and heading before it bakes, read at cd615a4. armature_rest_posture_quality finds hips, head and both feet (quality_role_map, score >= 0.55) and requires, in world space through matrix_world: head above hips, both feet below hips, world-Z alignment of (head minus hips) >= 0.58 (HRS_REST_BODY_VERTICAL_MIN) and of (hips minus foot) >= 0.50 (HRS_REST_LEG_VERTICAL_MIN). Failures read "Source armature rest pose is invalid: <issue>.For FBX, enable Automatic Bone Orientation; for BVH, verify the forward and up axes." or "Target armature rest pose is invalid: <issue>. Check the import axes or object rotation.", where <issue> is "The overall up direction is invalid", "The torso is nearly horizontal", "The leg direction deviates too far from the world Z axis" or "Could not identify a complete head, hips, and both feet structure". A yaw alignment of the source about the up axis is applied when both rigs yield anatomical axes (hips, head, and shoulders or upper legs) and the forward directions differ by at least 5 degrees (HRS_FORWARD_ALIGNMENT_MIN_DEGREES). The README's own limit: "Unusual rest poses or ambiguous forward axes may require cleanup before retargeting." Supporting evidence from this repo, read and not re-run: the five roles files scripts/bone_roles.py map wrote on 2026-09-16 record up +Z and forward -Y for every rig after Blender's FBX import, so these rigs stand upright in the sense the gate tests, though the gate itself was not run on them.
claims.as_first_reported: README limits: 'Severely incomplete humanoid rigs are rejected instead of being guessed.' and 'Unusual rest poses or ambiguous forward axes may require cleanup before retargeting.'

claims.candidate: Rig Bridge (Blender Extensions id humanoid_remap_studio; GitHub qw424886884/rig-bridge; by Feng Ji Shi)
claims.claim: How Rig Bridge copes with two rigs whose rest poses differ, read at cd615a4 and not run. The bake has two maths paths. The default is a rest-delta copy: per frame, source_delta = source_rest^-1 @ source_local for each mapped bone, rotation only (location only for hips), applied as target_rest @ target_delta; with scene.hrs_retarget_auto_rest_delta off it copies the raw local matrix instead. The second path, which the sweeper called "anatomical transfer", is used only when topology_fallback is true (either armature matched no preset) and hrs_retarget_auto_rest_delta is on (default True) and anatomical_transfer_context is ready: each side needs hips, spine_01, head, left_upper_leg and right_upper_leg among its mapped roles to build up, lateral and forward axes, then a per-role bone-direction frame from role pairs (upper_arm to lower_arm, lower_arm to hand, upper_leg to lower_leg, lower_leg to foot, foot to toe when present, hips to first spine, spine to spine to neck to head), and frames must exist for all 15 core roles on both sides; the target bone's rotation is then globalAlignment @ (source pose rotation @ source calibration) @ target calibration^-1, where each calibration is the rest rotation inverse times the direction frame, and hips translation is remapped through globalAlignment and scaled. Because bone_N names never match a preset, every retarget onto an articulationxl rig takes this anatomical path whenever the landmarks resolve, and falls back to the rest-delta copy when they do not, in which case a T-pose source onto an A-pose target would carry the rest-pose difference into the clip.
claims.as_first_reported: retarget.py keyframes per frame and, when either rig has no preset (topology_fallback) and scene.hrs_retarget_auto_rest_delta is on, uses an 'anatomical transfer' built from each rig's rest rotations and calibration frames.

checks.read: retarget.py lines 60 to 87 (pose_local_matrix, rest_local_matrix, rotation_only_delta), 88 to 237 (anatomical_* functions), 471 to 616 (both bake paths)
checks.evidence: topology_fallback = not armature_preset_profile(source) or not armature_preset_profile(target); anatomy_context = anatomical_transfer_context(source, target, pairs) if rest_delta_enabled and topology_fallback else {"ready": False}; required = {"hips", "spine_01", "head", "left_upper_leg", "right_upper_leg"}; "ready": not missing_core over CORE_REMAP_ROLE_IDS; anatomical_target_rotation returns context["globalAlignment"] @ (source_pose_rotation @ source_calibration) @ target_calibration.inverted_safe() with calibration = rest_rotation.inverted_safe() @ frame; hips translation = target head_local + globalAlignment @ source_motion * location_scale. Default path: source_delta = pair["source_rest"].inverted_safe() @ source_local if rest_delta_enabled else source_local; target_local = pair["target_rest"] @ rotation_only_delta(...).
checks.notes: One refinement: inside the anatomical path, a pair whose role has no direction frame on either side (anatomical_target_rotation returns None, for instance shoulders without a pair or finger chain bones) falls back per bone to the rest-delta copy, so the two paths can mix within one bake. The T-pose onto A-pose consequence is an inference from the maths, not something the repository states.

claims.candidate: Rig Bridge (Blender Extensions id humanoid_remap_studio; GitHub qw424886884/rig-bridge; by Feng Ji Shi)
claims.claim: Trial Rig Bridge 0.1.66 as the retarget step the note's "What to build" item 1 and VMC-050 describe, before writing a Copy Rotation retarget of this repo's own: it is GPL-3.0-or-later like ComfyUI and UniRig already in the image, carries no weights, body model, network or service terms, says nothing that reaches generated clips, and is the only tool read for this note built to recognise a rig without bone names. Do it on the CPU in the image's bpy 4.5.9: fetch the 86,851-byte zip by its sha256 at build time rather than vendoring it (CLAUDE.md), import the package and call register(), load one articulationxl FBX from output/rigged/ and one Mixamo FBX or a BVH, run set_scene_armature, auto_guess_pair, mapping_coverage and retarget_posture_gate, record scene.hrs_auto_detail and the per-role slot routes, then bake_retarget_action(scene) and inspect the Action with scripts/render_sheet.py --check. If the scan reports "No stable automatic workflow was found", write the bone names from the rig's roles file into hrs_mapping_slots with status "manual" and bake again. Treat it as a 0.1.x tool by one maintainer with no public test results: keep the retarget behind a script that can swap implementations, and if the trial fails on two rigs, fall back to building the role-keyed retarget VMC-050 describes. Unchecked: nothing was run.

Note item 1: "A BVH retarget onto articulationxl rigs, keyed on the roles scripts/bone_roles.py map writes: pair joints by role, drive each rig bone with Copy Rotation, bake". The premises checked here hold: GPL-3.0-or-later code, no weights, no network, no service terms, nothing about output, name-free topology route plus script-fillable slots.
checks.notes: A recommendation, so judged on its premises. Two adjustments for the trial script: bake_retarget_action does not run retarget_posture_gate itself, so the script must check the gate's result (the recommendation does list the call, but should act on "passed"); and the slot list has 37 roles. The claim that Rig Bridge is "the only tool read for this note built to recognise a rig without bone names" was not re-checked against every tool in the note; mesh2motion's retarget page uses a manual bone-mapping dialog per VMC-037, which is consistent with it.

claims.claim: As of 2026-10-02 at 3c4d5d7, read and not run: for each pair in src_skeleton.conversion_map(trg_skeleton), a dict keyed by the bound rig's bone name in which an empty slot on either side yields no entry, Bind creates a helper bone '<src_name>_RET' in the animated armature with the bound bone's rest head and tail (bone_utils.copy_bone_to_arm: 'trg_bone.head = src_bone.head_local; trg_bone.tail = src_bone.tail_local'), parents it under the mapped animated bone, moves it into the armature collection named by ret_bones_collection (default 'Retarget Bones', created with is_visible = False), and then adds constraints on the bound bone targeting that helper: COPY_ROTATION when rot_constraints (default True) and COPY_LOCATION when loc_constraints (default False); with loc_constraints off and bind_floating on (default), a bone with no binding constraint between it and the hips slot (is_bone_floating) gets both, so an unparented pelvis follows the hips' position. The code sets no target_space or owner_space, and Blender's DNA_constraint_types.h at v4.5.9 says of CONSTRAINT_SPACE_WORLD = 0: 'Default for all - world-space.' match_transform fixes the helper's rest orientation: 'None' (default) keeps the bound bone's own head and tail with a re-aligned roll, so each bound bone receives the animated bone's rotation relative to the two rigs' own rest poses and a constant rest-pose difference, such as arms at the sides against a T-pose, stays throughout the clip; 'Pose' ('Armature was posed manually to match rest pose of target') sets 'new_bone.matrix = ob.pose.bones[src_name].matrix', the bound rig's current pose, so a rig posed into the animated rig's rest pose before binding carries no such offset; 'Bone' ('Account for difference between control and deform rest pose (Requires similar proportions and Y bone-axis)') is for a control rig over a deform rig of one character; 'World' ('Just copy target world positions (Same bone orient, different rest pose)') gives the helper the animated bone's own head, tail and roll. fit_target_scale scales the animated armature by 'height_ratio = ob_height[2] / trg_height[2]' at the chosen spine slot (head, neck, spine2, spine1, spine or hips) and, with adjust_location (default True), divides its location keys by that ratio. A mapped bone missing from the animated armature is reported '{} not found in target' and skipped; a slot the bound rig lacks is simply unmapped, and since the helpers sit inside the animated hierarchy and the constraints copy world-space rotation, every mapped bone still takes its full world orientation.
